do you have a social contact?
I tried to make you join telegram: https://t.me/official_loonix
However, it seems like you don't use it.

I am in talks with @Samueru-sama along with several others, thinking how to go forward.
Would like to have your feedback, I scoured all the issues you created on many repos, and even your mastodon account, I have a general idea, but would like to have a more in depth talk, but github issue isn't realtime sadly.

Regarding this category, the [sbuild-linter](https://github.com/pkgforge/sbuilder) will auto add an `utility` category if one doesn't exist.
Otherwise, it's validated against this json: https://github.com/pkgforge/soarpkgs/blob/main/assets/category.json

But as you might have noticed, this entire repo will be changed significantly.
The main repo is https://github.com/pkgforge/soarpkgs
And this repo will just run the scripts from there and provide prebuilts.

Moreover, I added the tag field specifically because the official spec is too limited and it's not good for more refined filtering:
https://docs.pkgforge.dev/sbuild/specification/19.tag

---
### Lint Only
> For all cases
1. Download [Sbuild-linter](https://github.com/pkgforge/sbuilder)
```bash
$ sudo curl -qfsSL "https://api.gh.pkgforge.dev/repos/pkgforge/sbuilder/releases?per_page=100" \
| jq -r '.. | objects | .browser_download_url? // empty' | grep -Ei "$(uname -m)" | grep -Eiv "tar\.gz|\.b3sum" \
| grep -Ei "sbuild-linter" | sort --version-sort | tail -n 1 | tr -d '[:space:]' | xargs -I "{}" curl -qfsSL "{}" -o "./sbuild-linter"

$ chmod -v 'a+x' "./sbuild-linter"
```

2. Lint
```bash
$ ./sbuild-linter "./test.yaml" --pkgver
$ ./sbuild-linter test.yaml --pkgver
sbuild-linter v0.4.1
Linting test.yaml (/tmp/tmp.ofLKQOs0AK/test.yaml)

Performing shellcheck
[✔] Shellcheck passed

[+] 1 files validated successfully
[+] 0 files failed to pass validation
[+] Evaluated 1/1 file(s) in 475.886908ms
```
---
### Build
> Only if your SBUILD has little to no dependency
1. Download [Sbuild](https://github.com/pkgforge/sbuilder)
```bash
$ sudo curl -qfsSL "https://api.gh.pkgforge.dev/repos/pkgforge/sbuilder/releases?per_page=100" \
| jq -r '.. | objects | .browser_download_url? // empty' | grep -Ei "$(uname -m)" | grep -Eiv "tar\.gz|\.b3sum" \
| grep -Eiv "sbuild-linter" | sort --version-sort | tail -n 1 | tr -d '[:space:]' | xargs -I "{}" curl -qfsSL "{}" -o "./sbuild"

$ chmod -v 'a+x' "./sbuild"
```

2. Build
```bash
$ ./sbuild test.yaml --keep --log-level "verbose" --outdir "./test"
```

3. Check
```bash
$ ls "./test"
drwxrwxr-x 3 runner runner 220 Jan 16 01:38 github.com.flameshot-org.flameshot

$ ls test/github.com.flameshot-org.flameshot/

This one is a bit tricky.
While compiling git statically is possible, git will need some extra files & templates to work properly.
It will also expect all the helper binaries to be in `PATH` and the files to be in certain location.
This is to say, static git will require you to do some configuration by yourself.

I added a runimage version instead, which is a single file portable git, so if you are up for using that instead, I will go ahead and build it.

If FUSE is not installed, it cannot be used.
```sh
./nmap -sT -sC -sV 127.0.0.1
./nmap: failed to utilize FUSE during startup
Cannot mount RunImage, please check your FUSE setup.

You might still be able to extract the contents of this RunImage
if you run it with the --runtime-extract option
See https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageKit/wiki/FUSE
for more information

Timeout reached while waiting for mount: "/tmp/.r0/mnt/P1xSkS8k"
```

> If FUSE is not installed, it cannot be used.

Yes, this is a `runimage` & requires fuse.
You can still use it:
```bash
RUNTIME_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 ./nmap -sT -sC -sV 127.0.0.1
```

or 

```bash
"./nmap" --runtime-extract-and-run ${OPTIONS}
"./nmap" --runtime-extract-and-run -sT -sC -sV 127.0.0.1
```

In future versions, lack of fuse will be auto-detected and fallback will be used without users having to do it manually


---

As for a true static nmap, 
It won't work. It has too many dependencies now.
Previous versions were linked without lua and never supported nse.
So your only option is to use a `runimage`

body: By the way, I don't see the builds running on the RISC-V machine. Do we need to add a CI file for RISC-V builds, or is it already added?

> By the way, I don't see the builds running on the RISC-V machine. Do we need to add a CI file for RISC-V builds, or is it already added?

@alitariq4589 
Hi, currently all `riscv64-Linux` packages are built on GitHub runner `x86_64-Linux` through `QEMU` or Cross Compilation
The RISC-V machine you provided us is used for testing packages/scripts, not for CI.

There's now a section in the readme: https://github.com/pkgforge/soar#-sponsors
As for a blog, I will draft it in a few days.

Some updates:
There are three repos for `riscv64-Linux`
- https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/bincache (Limited support) [Packages: `612`]
- https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/external/pkgforge-cargo (Full Support) [Packages: `4363`]
- https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/external/pkgforge-go (Full Support) [Packages: `10146`]

Only `bincache` is manually curated, so the quality of packages from the other two repos may not be upto our usual standards.
Regardless, there's now `15,000` packages for `riscv64-Linux`

I will figure out the docker and the missing repos in the coming weeks.

Building these many packages for RISC-V is really valuable to us. We are constantly adding new RISC-V boards in the platform as they arrive (see our [list of compute instances](https://10x-engineers.github.io/riscv-ci-partners/compute_instances/)).

In the meantime, I would also like to study the packages included in the builds, where the source code is hosted, etc. It would be great if you could point me in the right direction.

> If you need anything from my side

Unfortunately, it is not possible to set up proper CI without root access.
And as described in: https://github.com/pkgforge/soarpkgs/discussions/197#discussioncomment-13357660, offering us root inside a rootless Podman container, that can also run docker inside, is the only way for runners to be provisioned.


I have been [restructuring](https://github.com/pkgforge/soarpkgs/commit/c1be5654e6d4f2afee3eada72a232b13c62e82b7) how our Build scripts work, so they can be cross compiled due to the limitation above.
As well as creating new repos like [pkgforge-cargo](https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/external/pkgforge-cargo) & [pkgforge-go](https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/external/pkgforge-go) which build the packages for riscv64 via cross compilation.

> I would also like to study the packages included in the builds

If you prefer docs, then https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/bincache, https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/external/pkgforge-cargo & https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/external/pkgforge-go should contain all the information you are looking for

However, a better way would be to:
1. [Install Soar](https://github.com/pkgforge/soar)
```bash
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pkgforge/soar/main/install.sh" | sh
```
2. Configure Soar (This won't be necessary in a future version)
```bash
$ soar defconfig #populates a default config at "${HOME}/.soar/config.toml"

#Add these at end to "${HOME}/.soar/config.toml"
[[repositories]]
name = "pkgforge-cargo"
url = "https://meta.pkgforge.dev/external/pkgforge-cargo/riscv64-Linux.json.zstd"
desktop_integration = false
signature_verification = false
sync_interval = "3h"

[[repositories]]
name = "pkgforge-go"
url = "https://meta.pkgforge.dev/external/pkgforge-go/riscv64-Linux.json.zstd"
desktop_integration = false
signature_verification = false
sync_interval = "3h"

$ soar sync
```

3. List All Packages
```bash
#This will list all the packages the repos you configured have
soar list
```

4. Query everything about a Package
```bash
#Find a package you are interested in
#We use flatpak style pkg_id because we have too many packages and to ensure packages don't overwrite each other
#Example, soar for micro, a text editor
$ soar search micro --limit 1000
[-] micro#github.com_zyedidia_micro:pkgforge-go | HEAD-97b5e35-250620T210025:nightly | static - A modern and intuitive terminal-based text editor (13.08 MiB)

#Query it
soar query "micro#github.com_zyedidia_micro:pkgforge-go"
```
> where the source code is hosted

1. Source code for CI/Infra?
> - https://github.com/pkgforge/bincache/tree/main/scripts
> - https://github.com/pkgforge/bincache/tree/main/.github/workflows
> - https://github.com/pkgforge-cargo/builder/tree/main/scripts
> - https://github.com/pkgforge-cargo/builder/tree/main/.github/workflows
> - https://github.com/pkgforge-go/builder/tree/main/scripts
> - https://github.com/pkgforge-go/builder/tree/main/.github/workflows
> - More details and extra information is available at: https://docs.pkgforge.dev

2. Build Scripts (Applies only to our official repos)
```bash
$ soar inspect "${PKG_NAME}"

#Example
soar inspect "bash#nixpkgs.bash:bincache" | less
```
> This is not available for external repos like pkgforge-cargo/pkgforge-go because a single build script builds all packages automagically

3. Build Logs (Available for all packages)
```bash
$ soar log "${PKG_NAME}"

#Example
soar log "micro#github.com_zyedidia_micro:pkgforge-go" | less
```

Also, I constantly get bombarded with GitHub notifications, so I don't see them.

This doesn't start Docker inside the podman for reduced overhead, but this does have sudo installed inside it. The GitHub Actions package runs without elevated permissions, but you can use passwordless sudo for tasks that require elevated permissions. Let me know if you see any issues with this setup.

loginctl enable-linger $USER
podman system migrate
```

After this, you can test Podman on your user account on the provided RISC-V machine.

Addressed all points in the review:

**1. Builds in CI now** — [`sharno/IriunWebcam-AppImage`](https://github.com/sharno/IriunWebcam-AppImage) was rebuilt on the [Anylinux-AppImages](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages) template ([commit](https://github.com/sharno/IriunWebcam-AppImage/commit/7ab4309)):
- `.github/workflows/appimage.yml` builds in the `ghcr.io/pkgforge-dev/archlinux` container via `anylinux-setup-action`, on a 21-day cron + `workflow_dispatch`
- `make-appimage.sh` fetches the version from https://iriun.gitlab.io at build time, pulls the upstream deb, and deploys with `quick-sharun` (Qt6 plugins + all transitive libs auto-deployed; the `iriunaudio` SPA plugin and `pipewire.conf.d` shipped via `ADD_DIR`) — no `onelf`, no manual `appimagetool` invocation, nothing machine-dependent
- released with `make-stable-appimage-release` → tag `2.9.3@2026-08-29_1787976881`, artifact `IriunWebcam-2.9.3-anylinux-x86_64.AppImage` (34.7 MiB, DWARFS, sharun + uruntime — works on musl/non-FHS hosts, no host Qt)
- first CI run green end-to-end, and the scheduled rebuild handles future bumps

**2. Re-pinned** — [`iriunwebcam-2.9.3.toml`](https://github.com/sharno/soarpkgs/commit/827d9747) now pins the CI-built artifact (blake3 `7e5dfe5b…`, sha256 `27de3235…`, 34687557 bytes), and `pkg.toml` uses `tag-suffix = "strip"` for the `VERSION@DATE` tag format like `discord`.

**3. Committed AppImage dropped** — the 40 MiB `IriunWebcam-2.9.3-x86_64.AppImage` is removed from the appimage repo; the artifact only exists as a CI release now.
